title: Why performing is the happiest moment
summary: Ted Jr. and Hinton say the world falls away once the music starts.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: When you get into the performance like I saw with these people, they are inspired and they're happy, and I feel the same way. The happiest moments of my life was when we played, not particularly for me on the bass, but when the three of us played together at Wolf Trap or Underground or anywhere, but when we were playing music, all of a sudden, all the world was gone and I was happier probably than anybody in this world.
And of course, being and playing with Dad, too. But the whole spirit -- you're always
inspired; it makes you accomplish things that you never thought you could do. So that -- whenever the performance is on for me, that's my happiest moment.
Sure. Like when I hit that bandstand and start playing, that's my world and I'm happy. My security blanket is my fiddle. If everything else fails, the fiddle lifts me out.

I've gone to a gig and I've had a miserable day and a lot of things are on my mind, and the politics -- and start that set, everything is cleared out, and for hours afterwards, even, I'm still just -- like I was on my deathbed and now I'm read to run in the Olympics. It's great.
